svg.title: Agent Evaluation & Observability
svg.desc: Proposed evaluation and observability design for the Enterprise AI Agent Sales and Risk System. This is an architecture design, not an implemented evaluation service or measured improvement claim. The online path instruments asynchronous LangGraph draft and revision jobs on AWS Bedrock AgentCore Runtime with OpenTelemetry and ADOT. Trace Collection begins at enqueue/dispatch and follows queue wait, execution, retries, both agent branches, retrieval, SQL calculations, validation, draft persistence and manager review. It includes failed and abandoned jobs, not only completed chatbot responses. A job/revision may contain multiple correlated traces and spans; parent run, retry attempt and idempotency keys link them without treating every message as a new unrelated session. Correlation includes authenticated customer/project, session, request, draft revision/hash, source snapshot, model, prompt, graph, calculation and application versions. Sensitive payloads are redacted and telemetry access is scoped. CloudWatch and AgentCore Observability are the primary operational telemetry destination. Online Monitoring measures latency, queue age, draft-ready latency, errors, retries, token usage and estimated cost per completed job and revision, including failed attempts, both agents and evaluator calls. Duplicate commits, stuck jobs, stale results and job completion status are also monitored. Job retries are not new successful drafts. Cost estimates are not billing guarantees or hard budget enforcement. Optional sampled quality evaluation uses AgentCore Evaluations and does not block each reply. Monitoring and quality evaluation are parallel consumers of traces, not sequential dependencies. Human Failure Review selects confirmed failures and representative cases; production outputs are never automatically promoted to ground truth. The Manager Feedback Loop starts with a Versioned Draft. Reject/Edit Feedback records the manager's reason, selected option, old and new input values, diff, reviewer authority, draft and job/revision IDs and source manifest. Every feedback event is recorded, including feedback that is not promoted to an evaluation case. Rejection alone is not evidence of agent failure. Evidence and Change Review checks source facts, access scope and timestamps, with a human reviewer classifying agent error, verified new information, policy/preference changes or unresolved disagreement. Feedback is not automatically a correct label, and the evaluator does not silently change authoritative costs from a manager's comment. Only reviewed cases with verified expected behavior enter the dataset, linked to before/after draft and source versions. A new design version is an input update, whereas ignoring an available design version may be a retrieval/reasoning error. The production Multi-Agent workflow owns targeted recalculation and re-approval; this eval diagram only captures and tests that behavior. Neither feedback nor a release gate automatically updates model weights or sends customer quotes. Human-reviewed feedback and operational cases enter an access-controlled, versioned evaluation dataset in Snowflake, with larger evidence snapshots and artifacts in S3. MLflow records feedback assessments linked to the originating trace. Datasets include expected evidence IDs, deterministic pricing outcomes, approved inputs, dependency expectations, units, currencies, effective source versions and approval requirements. Cases cover cost, quantity and design changes; normal questions; rejection without error; missing sources; customer isolation; revoked ACLs; stale versions; retries; duplicates; tool failures and prompt injection. Customer data remains permission scoped, with separate development and final holdout sets and no cross-split near-duplicate feedback threads. Human-reviewed labels and judge rubrics are versioned. Candidate Runs execute the new agent application against pinned inputs and data snapshots. Re-scoring an old trace alone does not establish that new application behavior improved. The Evaluation Suite has four independent categories, implemented with pytest/custom evaluation code and recorded in MLflow. MLflow is the experiment/trace/assessment record, not the tool that automatically enforces deployment permission. RAG Retrieval Tests use human-reviewed relevant evidence labels for Recall@k and ranking/context precision, and explicit negative tests for cross-customer/project leakage, missing document ACLs, revocations, stale sources and prompt injection. Zero observed leaks in a test corpus is a release requirement, not a mathematical proof of universal isolation. Quote Calculation Tests compare tool outputs with independently verified expected values and approved pricing rules. They test cost, quantity tiers, design/BOM versions, one-time charge allocation, margins, currency, units and rounding. An LLM judge cannot certify numerical correctness or replace an independently checked calculation oracle. Recalculation Tests replay cost, quantity and design changes as paired before/after scenarios. A reference full recompute under the same approved inputs validates deterministic numbers, source dependencies and policy outcomes from the targeted recompute, within declared numeric tolerances. Textual LLM outputs need not match word-for-word. Tests verify that all affected nodes run, unchanged nodes are reused only with matching dependencies, sources refresh correctly, obsolete jobs cannot overwrite newer drafts, retries do not duplicate commits, stale approval is invalidated, new drafts require review and unchanged explanation/comparison questions do not trigger needless full-agent reruns. Agent Quality Tests measure evidence-supported claims, citation correctness, task completion, required business and engineering handoffs, conflict handling, appropriate abstention and calibrated human-reviewed LLM judging. Report critical slices separately; semantic faithfulness alone does not imply the source is correct or the price is commercially valid. Agent tests also verify use of the approved risk-model tool and score snapshot. Predictive ML model evaluation is separate, in Risk Model Training and Eval before registry promotion; it measures precision, recall, calibration and lead time on time-based holdouts, with drift monitoring after deployment. Version Comparison compares candidate and baseline on the same dataset, with critical slices and quality, latency and cost. The Release Gate is implemented by test assertions, threshold policies, required CI checks and protected deployment jobs in GitHub Actions. MLflow supplies evaluation records rather than independently enforcing deployment permissions. Agent application releases and predictive model promotions have distinct version identifiers and acceptance criteria. A failed gate requires an explicit candidate revision and re-run; it does not automatically edit prompts or update weights. A passing gate permits a staged release, subject to protected deployment approval, monitoring and rollback procedures. The continuous return of deployed traffic to online monitoring is abstracted to avoid a perimeter feedback arrow. This is software and model release approval; customer quote approval remains a separate runtime business workflow. Enterprise-approved model, region, retention and logging policies cover evaluator calls as well as production inference. The four later UI entry points remain Trace Explorer, Evaluation Results, Version Comparison and Release Decision. Brand marks retain their native colors, with consistently sized 32-pixel logo frames. Other diagrams remain unchanged.
